_note: Documentation-verified. The smoke column of the record is still empty; nothing here may be treated as proven until it is filled.
_gptSizeRule: Arbitrary WIDTHxHEIGHT is gpt-image-2 and the two 2.5 models only; both edges divisible by 16, aspect between 1:3 and 3:1, neither edge over 3840, and TOTAL PIXELS between 655,360 and 8,294,400 inclusive. gpt-image-1.5 accepts ONLY the three standard sizes, so every resolution collapses to the nearest standard one. Verified 2026-09-22 against the size validator in platform.openai.com/docs/guides/image-generation.
_fluxSizeRule: fal-ai/flux-2 takes image_size as {width,height} with BOTH edges clamped to 512-2048. It does NOT accept aspect_ratio. The 2048 ceiling means only 1:1 can actually reach 4MP; 16:9 tops out at 2.36MP. Retail is a flat price per tier (see fluxTierUsd), so the 4MP tier is WITHHELD at every non-square ratio rather than sold at a size the endpoint cannot produce - resolutionExclusions on the flux family, enforced in request-validation. The dimension table lives in the catalog (model-families FLUX_DIMS) because the request builder reads it; duplicating it here would let the offer and the request drift.
_fluxProviderRate: fal quotes $0.012 per megapixel on the flux-2 model page (documentation only, never seen on an invoice). Retail does NOT track it; the flat tiers below are the deliberate price.
_seedreamSizeRule: image_size accepts auto, auto_2K, auto_4K and the preset enums, or {width,height}; total pixels between 960x960 and 4096x4096. No aspect_ratio parameter, so a non-square ratio must be sent as explicit dimensions.
_nanoFastNote: Repointed 2026-09-22. It was gemini-2.5-flash-image, which Google's pricing page marks deprecated with a shutdown on 2026-10-02: every request on the fast tier would have started failing on that date. Nano Banana 2 Lite is the migration Google names. Published rate: $30/1M image output tokens, 1120 tokens for a 1K image, = $0.0336 per image.
_gptVersionNote: 2026-09-22: gpt-image-1 removed from the offer (owner decision). The two GPT Image 2.5 models added: flare is 'our fastest model for high-quality, everyday image generation', sunburst is 'our most capable model for image generation and editing... where editing precision matters most' (platform.openai.com/docs/models). Both support low, medium, high, xhigh, max and auto; we expose only low/medium/high because qualities are a family-level capability and gpt-image-1.5 and 2 do not accept xhigh or max.
_gptSizeFix: 2026-09-22: 16:9:1K and 9:16:1K were 1024x576 / 576x1024 = 589,824 px, BELOW the 655,360 minimum, so the validator rejects them outright. 1280x720 / 720x1280 (921,600 px) is the smallest 16:9 pair that clears the floor with both edges divisible by 16. This was an ordinary 16:9-at-1K request on the default version of a live family. Never observed failing against the live API - found by driving the documented validator - so one real 16:9 1K generation is still owed as proof.
_gptQualityRule: low/medium/high on gpt-image-2 and gpt-image-1.5; the 2.5 models add xhigh and max. The guide is explicit: 'For gpt-image-2, the options are low, medium, and high.' Enforced by capabilities.versionQualities in the catalog and by validateSettings.
